data.name: Hibat
data.gender_notes: Hibat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hibat is an Arabic name that means 'gift'. It is a unisex name and is mentioned in the Quran. The name is often given to children born after a long wait, as a symbol of the parents' gift from Allah. The name Hibat carries the meaning “Gift” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Hibat usually hope their child will grow to embody gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A gift from Allah, symbolizing patience and gratitude.
data.etymology: Hibat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hibat total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Hibat
in_english.meaning: human's complete submission and obedience to Allah
in_english.long_meaning: Hibat is an important concept in Islam that refers to a person's complete submission and obedience to Allah. It is a fundamental aspect of a Muslim's faith and is considered a necessary step in achieving spiritual growth and development. The term hibat is derived from the Arabic root 'h-b-t', which means 'to submit' or 'to obey'. In Islamic theology, hibat is seen as a means of purifying one's soul and seeking closeness to Allah. It involves surrendering one's will to Allah's will and submitting to His commands. A person who practices hibat is considered to be in a state of complete surrender to Allah, which is seen as a sign of spiritual maturity and wisdom. Hibat is also associated with the concept of 'tawbah', or repentance, which is an essential aspect of Islamic spirituality.

In some communities, a child born after a long wait is given the name as a symbol of the parents' gratitude and blessing. The name is also associated with the idea of giving and receiving gifts, reflecting the importance of generosity, kindness and gratitude in Islam.

The name reminds us of the greatest gift of all - the gift of faith and the blessings of Allah. In the Quran, Allah says, "And [recall] when your Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves [saying]: 'Am I not your Lord?' they said, 'Yes, we have testified.' [This] - lest you should say on the day of contemplation, 'Of this we were never habitants.' Basic notions about short messages. Dost thou not remember? So he whom Allah had granted to reason or a sense of self, will find a way out, and he whom Allah had left astray, will be accounted a loser." (Al-A'raf 7:172-173). This passage highlights the importance of recognizing and accepting Allah as our Creator and Sustainer, and reminds us of the spiritual gift of reason, intellect, and the ability to choose between right and wrong. The name Hibat thus carries a reminder of the spiritual journey and the gift of self-awareness, intellect and reason, as well as the blessings of Allah.
